rows.requirement: After source repair and before real refitting:
Run the original required mathematical and numerical gates.
- Original exact model equations B0–B4, D, C, S.
- Original PG, AD and finite-difference acceptance thresholds.
Revalidate actual integration of corrected inputs into the frozen production worker.
Ordinary implementation defects may be repaired before scientific attempts, with independent regressions.
Do not change mathematical objectives, solver tolerances or optimization budgets to force a PASS.
Create a versioned corrective execution ledger.
- Maximum 61 fresh A attempts per corrected eligible Development mouse.
- If exactly 10 mice qualify, maximum MAIN attempts: 610.
- Maximum five B0–B4 fits per applicable case per eligible Development mouse.
- Absolute new Development sensitivity cap: 660 attempts.
- Only the original four fixed 999-replicate reference suites.
- No additional model fitting for these suites.
Every fresh fit has one original configuration, original start policy and no retries.
Do not initialize corrected fits from historical rounded-input coefficients.
No new seeds, solver budgets, favorable retry or post-result selection.
Log historical plus new attempt totals separately and cumulatively.
This new budget is explicitly authorized as a corrective execution amendment. It does not retrospectively assert compliance with the original aggregate attempt ceiling.
Stop at the caps; do not request another expansion automatically.
Only after the complete repaired input and production certification passes:
A. Execute the fresh authorized Development A baseline and D/C/S fits.
B. Independently verify all required numerical results and failure journals.
C. Freeze eligible global model and hyperparameter choices using Development B only.
D. Register and execute the originally frozen Development sensitivity fits within the new budget.
E. Freeze the required E-batch implementation and control configuration.
F. Evaluate Development E once, producing all registered exploratory comparisons and controls.
Development E outcomes must never influence model selection, source/QC thresholds, feature construction or new scientific amendments.
Do not create a model winner before B selection is complete.
Failures and negative results are scientifically acceptable outputs.
Use exact scored nominal unit-bin denominators and equal-mouse aggregation.
Apply the frozen uncertainty and statistical procedures only to legitimately completed results.
Report all negative, mixed, failed, missing or inconclusive outcomes.
Do not promote Development results to independent held-out confirmation.
Do not claim biological discrete primitives, neural mechanisms, movement independence or CWP/NAP ontology validation.
If the final Development stage is scientifically incomplete, deliver a truthful STOP report.
Reuse compatible existing source readers, source inventories, math workers, synthetic tests and independent review evidence.
Do not rerun unrelated data-source investigations.
Avoid rebuilding an entire engineering framework around one timestamp serialization defect.
